items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The Musical World of J. J. Johnson by Joshua Berrett and Louis Bourgois III

ctx.x: That was the second album, yeah. Eurosuite came about under interesting circumstances. Classical pianist Friedrich Gulda was also a very good jazz pianist and had a keen interest in jazz, even though his forte was as a classical musician and as a

classical pianist. But he put together a jazz band to tour in Europe. I don’t know what year that was. [In the discography of The Musical World of J. J. Johnson by Joshua Berrett and Louis Bourgois III there is a listing for two days of recording on September 13-14, 1965 in Vienna, Austria by Friedrich Gulda and His Euro-Orchestra; both J. J. Johnson and Freddie Hubbard are listed in the personnel.] Dave, what [was the] approximate . . .
I just remember you and Freddie [Hubbard] were two of the main soloists on it.
